content:
A common application of Zorn's lemma is this:

Suppose I want to construct a FooHom from FooSource to FooTarget. Consider that partial FooHoms whose domain is a SubFoo of FooSource and whose codomain is still FooTarget. These form a partial order by taking f ≤ g to mean f.dom ≤ g.dom and g agrees with f wherever f is defined. This partial order has suprema for directed sets (in particular nonempty chains) because the Foo operations are finitary. This partial order is nonempty because it contains the trivial FooHom whose domain is (⊥ : SubFoo FooSource), so by Zorn's lemma it has a maximal element. Then the domain of this maximal partial function must be (⊤ : SubFoo FooSource), because if it was some dom ≠ ⊤ then I find some x ∉ dom and extend it to another FooHom with domain SubFoo.closure (insert x ↑dom), which would contradict maximality.

This argument works whenever Foo has only finitary operations and whenever I can build a FooHom (⊥ : SubFoo FooSource) FooTarget and I can extend a FooHom dom FooTarget to a FooHom (SubFoo.closure (insert x ↑dom)) FooTarget. But to carry out this argument in Lean, I need to build the type of partial FooHoms and define a PartialOrder instance and prove it has directed suprema, and this construction is carried out at least three different times in mathlib with different values of Foo, which seems like a lot of duplication to me. Surely there's a better way to do this?

This feels related to https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Abstracting.20the.20substructure.20lattice.20construction/with/607025739
Morally if not mathematically
perhaps we need a typeclass for "the directed union of SubFoos is another SubFoo"
though I guess this wouldn't work for file#Topology/ShrinkingLemma, where it's not so clear what Foo actually is
Can you point to the concrete cases? I am aware of docs#LinearPMap, but I don't know which are the other ones.
For docs#IntermediateField.Lifts and docs#LinearPMap, I would expect there is a common abstraction that is not too difficult to implement

I have been saying before but not yet implemented it: We should have a version of Zorn that works for (unbundled) subtypes of complete lattices (ie we are given a complete lattice \alpha and a predicate p : \alpha -> Prop and the fact that if s : Set \alpha is a chain and \forall x \in s, p x then p (sSup s)). This covers (almost?) all uses of Zorn in mathlib

I think what we actually want is "the directed union commutes with the forgetful map SetLike.coe" ie IsConcreteCsSup
